samples.summary: Third hand-rolled glob→RegExp engine added, duplicating the repo's designated shared one
samples.evidence:
`CI_DEFINING_RE` (checks.mjs:140-153) compiles the `CI_DEFINING_PATHS` globs with a fresh, inline `**`/`*` → RegExp translation. Two implementations of exactly this already exist and one is explicitly designated as the shared home:

- `scripts/agent/review-panel.mjs:198` `export function globToRegExp(glob)` — same directory as checks.mjs, and `scripts/agent/hunt-gate.mjs:46-51` says in prose "What IS safely shared, because it is polarity-neutral: … `globToRegExp` from review-panel.mjs" and imports it. The SDK is loaded lazily there precisely so the pure helpers stay importable.
- `scripts/changed-areas.mjs:56` `export function globToRegExp(glob)` — "Glob → RegExp, supporting exactly what the config uses: `*` within a path segment and `**` across segments", and `matchesAny` (line 84) applies it to `ci.ciConfig`, i.e. to *the very same glob list* checks.mjs now mirrors (`harness.config.json:52-62`).

The three are not equivalent: changed-areas special-cases `**/` as `(?:.*/)?`, review-panel emits `.*` for `**` and also supports `?`, the new copy splits on `**` and joins with `.*` with a different escape set. So the repo now has two different answers to "does this path match a `ciConfig` glob" — `changed-areas.resolve()` decides whether CI runs in full, `definesCi()` decides whether the ready gate refuses to promote. The new copy is a stated REFUSAL surface ("a pattern that accidentally matched less is a fail-open"), and the drift test added in `checks.test.mjs` only asserts list *membership* against `ciConfig`, never that the two matchers classify a path the same way. The hard-coding of the list is justified in the comment by provenance (default-branch checkout); nothing justifies re-implementing the matcher rather than importing `globToRegExp`.

samples.summary: Design doc added by this change states capture-collect.yml is unguarded, while the same change guards it
samples.evidence: The doc hunk adds: "**`capture-collect.yml` is the same class and is NOT yet guarded** — an open gap … It consumes `workflow_run` by display name … with no `path`, branch or head-repository clause … Closing it needs the same one-line `github.event.workflow_run.path` clause on that job's `if:`, matched against the two producer files instead of `ci.yml`, and it needs a MAINTAINER". The same diff adds exactly that clause plus the head-repository clause to `.github/workflows/capture-collect.yml:139-143` (verified in the working tree). The doc therefore records a closed hole as an open one and prescribes work already done, and the parenthetical about needing a maintainer is contradicted by the change itself. A design doc that describes a security posture the code no longer has is the kind of stale record `CONTRIBUTING.md`'s design-doc discipline exists to prevent.

samples.summary: Stale 'What gate 1 does NOT prove' paragraph contradicts gate 1b added in the same change
samples.evidence: Lines 2011-2018 state: "a branch able to edit that file can produce a genuinely green run at the genuine path with no tests in it … Gate 1 therefore means 'a separate actor reports CI green for this SHA', not 'main's CI definition passed'; closing that needs the run's workflow content compared against the base branch." The same doc hunk, ~100 lines earlier ("**Gate 1b: WHICH file ran is not WHAT was in it.**"), and `mark-ready.mjs:236-288` do close exactly this by refusing any PR that supplies a CI-defining path. Two paragraphs of the same section now give opposite answers on whether the gap is open, and the later one prescribes a different remedy than the one shipped. Fold the residual-risk statement into the gate 1b section rather than leaving a parallel, superseded account.

samples.summary: Gate 1b makes auto-promotion unreachable for a common and important PR class (dependency bumps, harness self-changes)
samples.evidence: `CI_DEFINING_PATHS` (checks.mjs:123-135) includes `package.json`, `packages/*/package.json`, `pnpm-lock.yaml`, `pnpm-workspace.yaml` and `.github/workflows/**`. Any PR that adds a dependency, adds a package script, or touches the harness — which is a large share of this repo's agent-authored work, this change included — can now never satisfy the ready gate and will sit as a draft until a human flips it. The doc calls this out ("Such a PR is not blocked, only un-automated"), so it is a conscious trade, but it materially narrows the stated outcome of the agentic loop (`docs/design/harness-engineering.md`'s autonomous draft→ready promotion) and there is no escape hatch (no `--allow-ci-config` opt-in analogous to `--allow-no-checks` at mark-ready.mjs:104). Worth an explicit decision record, or a narrower surface (e.g. lockfile-only changes), rather than blanket refusal.

samples.summary: The `@ref`-stripping regression is narrated twice in adjacent paragraphs
samples.evidence: Lines 1963-1972 ("Do NOT restore an `@ref` tolerance …") and lines 1974-1982 ("**Gate 1 identifies CI by asking the API for that workflow's runs** … the first attempt stripped an `@ref` suffix …") tell the same story with the same reasoning, including the same awkward prose workaround for the doc-staleness backtick gate. One of the two should go; the section is already very long and duplicated narrative is what rots first.

samples.summary: The change bundles five independent concerns into one review unit
samples.evidence: The diff mixes: (1) `workflow_run.path` gating across four workflows, (2) a new check-run producer filter (`CHECK_PRODUCER_APP_SLUG`), (3) an entirely new promotion gate 1b with base/head pinning and file-list pagination, (4) a shell exit-code `case` refactor plus a new `outcome` vocabulary shared with loop-status, and (5) pagination of the `@claude rerun` run selection. No originating issue was supplied with this review, so I cannot check any of these against an `acceptance` list; flagged only because each is separately revertible and (3) in particular changes promotion policy for every PR, which is the kind of decision that reads better on its own.

finding.summary: Third hand-rolled glob→RegExp engine added, duplicating the repo's designated shared one
finding.evidence:
`CI_DEFINING_RE` (checks.mjs:140-153) compiles the `CI_DEFINING_PATHS` globs with a fresh, inline `**`/`*` → RegExp translation. Two implementations of exactly this already exist and one is explicitly designated as the shared home:

- `scripts/changed-areas.mjs:56` `export function globToRegExp(glob)` — "Glob → RegExp, supporting exactly what the config uses: `*` within a path segment and `**` across segments", and `matchesAny` (line 84) applies it to `ci.ciConfig`, i.e. to *the very same glob list* checks.mjs now mirrors (`harness.config.json:52-62`).

verdict.reason: The inline matcher is genuinely present (checks.mjs:137-159) and globToRegExp does exist in two other places, so the duplication observation is factually real — but it is minor, not blocking, under this lens's rubric. (1) No divergence exists: tracing every pattern in checks.mjs:123-135 and harness.config.json:52-62, none contains `?` or a mid-pattern `**/`, so the inline compiler, review-panel.mjs:198-208 and changed-areas.mjs:56-82 all compile byte-identical regexes; the two matchers give the SAME answer for every glob either list holds today. (2) The reviewer's remedy would not fix the cited hazard anyway: the two existing exports already disagree with each other (review-panel maps `?`→[^/] and any `**`→`.*`; changed-areas escapes `?` literally and maps `**/`→`(?:.*/)?`), so importing review-panel's copy would still not make definesCi agree with changed-areas.resolve(). The three-way disagreement pre-exists and is not created here. (3) The matcher's behavior IS pinned: checks.test.mjs:514-548 asserts definesCi's classification for 13 gating paths and 8 negatives, so the finding's claim that the test checks only list membership is incomplete. Result: the change works exactly as specified, no acceptance criterion is unmet, and the cost stays inside the codebase (latent drift if a `**/`-shaped ciConfig entry is ever added). The rubric states that a discipline violation leaving the change working as specified is not `major`, and files "reuse that was available but not required" under minor — which never blocks.

finding.summary: Gate 1b is unrequested scope well past the issue's stated Non-goal, and it changes who gets auto-promoted
finding.evidence:
The originating task (`docs/tasks/active/20260825-promote-exit-code-default-todo.md`, "Promote job: close mark-ready's exit-code chain (#937)") states its Non-goals as "No change to `mark-ready.mjs`'s behavior or its exit-code numbering. The script's contract is already what #929 pinned; only the consumer and the tests change." Its "Scope added after review" section enumerates exactly four post-review additions (identify CI by path, keep newest-wins, guard the trigger side, record `outcome`) — gate 1b is not among them, nor is the base-branch pinning or the head-re-read.

This diff nevertheless adds an entirely new promotion gate to `mark-ready.mjs`: `ciDefiningPathsChanged()` + `defaultBranch()` + `ranBaseCiDefinition()` (`scripts/agent/mark-ready.mjs:180-259`), wired in as `const ciDefinitionGate = ranBaseCiDefinition(prNumber);` and added to the `gates` array as "CI's definition came from main". The cost is operational, not tidiness: `CI_DEFINING_PATHS` includes `package.json`, `packages/*/package.json`, `pnpm-lock.yaml`, `pnpm-workspace.yaml` and `knip.json`, so every dependency-touching agent PR — a routine class — silently loses auto-promotion, as does any PR whose base is not the repository default branch (stacked/agent-chained PRs), all shipped inside a fix for an exit-code `if`-chain. The behavior is documented in `docs/design/harness-engineering.md`, but not sanctioned by the issue this branch claims.

verdict.reason: Verified all three factual pillars. (1) Gate 1b is present and unconditionally reachable in mark-ready.mjs: header docs at :19-43, ciDefiningPathsChanged() at :205, defaultBranch() at :228, ranBaseCiDefinition() at :236, invoked at :288 and pushed into the `gates` array at :324, with `gates.every` at :337 gating promotion and exit 1 at :341. The reviewer's line range (180-259) is offset from the actual 195-288, but every named function and the wiring exist. (2) The refusal surface is as described: CI_DEFINING_PATHS at checks.mjs:123-135 lists package.json, packages/*/package.json, pnpm-lock.yaml, pnpm-workspace.yaml and knip.json, matched via definesCi() (:156) against both filename and previous_filename, so any dependency-touching PR returns false at :271; the base-branch pin at mark-ready.mjs:244 additionally refuses any PR not targeting the default branch (stacked/retargeted PRs). (3) The Non-goal is quoted accurately at todo:77-81, and the "Scope added after review" list at todo:47-76 enumerates exactly the four items the reviewer names, with gate 1b, the base pin and the head re-read absent. The lessons file (:177-195, "Round 4") confirms gate 1b was authored and iterated on this task, so this is not pre-existing code. No refutation ground applies: the code is present (not not-present), no caller or guard makes it unreachable (not already-guarded), and scope past a stated Non-Goal with an operational cost — routine dependency-touching and non-default-base agent PRs silently losing auto-promotion — is squarely inside the design-fit lens's rubric for `major` (not out-of-scope). The todo's own preamble at :49-53 sanctioning panel-driven departures from the Non-goal is mitigating but does not cover 1b, whose enumeration is explicit; that ambiguity is a reason to keep the finding, not drop it.

finding.summary: Third, semantically different glob→RegExp engine added where the repo already has one that interprets the very globs being mirrored
finding.evidence:
`CI_DEFINING_RE` in `scripts/agent/checks.mjs:140-153` hand-rolls glob→RegExp a third time. `scripts/changed-areas.mjs:56` already exports `globToRegExp` — and it is *the* matcher that interprets `harness.config.json`'s `ci.ciConfig`, the list `CI_DEFINING_PATHS` claims to mirror (`scripts/changed-areas.mjs:84 matchesAny`, used by `classify()` to compute `ciConfig`). `scripts/agent/review-panel.mjs:198` has a second copy, and `.github/workflows/ci-report.yml:217` a third — but that one is explicitly justified ("this workflow deliberately checks out no code") and is pinned against the module by `scripts/test/ci-workflow.test.mjs:154`. `checks.mjs` runs with a checkout and already imports freely, so no such justification applies, and the new copy is pinned against nothing.

The two engines are not equivalent: `changed-areas.mjs` renders `**/` as `(?:.*/)?` (matches zero intermediate directories), while the new one splits on `**` and joins with `.*`, so `packages/**/package.json` would match `packages/a/package.json` in both but `packages/package.json` only in the former. Adding any such glob to `ci.ciConfig` therefore gives two different answers to "does this path define CI" — CI forces a full run while gate 1b waves the PR through. The direction of divergence is fail-open on a gate whose own comment calls itself "a REFUSAL surface, so a pattern that accidentally matched less is a fail-open".

verdict.reason: The third glob compiler does exist (scripts/agent/checks.mjs:140-153) and scripts/changed-areas.mjs:56-82 does export globToRegExp, so the reuse observation is factually real. But the claimed blocking cost — "two different answers to 'does this path define CI'", fail-open on gate 1b — does not exist in this tree. Every glob on the live surface (harness.config.json:52-62 ci.ciConfig; CI_DEFINING_PATHS at checks.mjs:123-135) is trailing-`**`, single-`*`, or literal, and on exactly those shapes the two compilers produce equivalent regexes (trailing `**`→`.*`, `*`→`[^/]*`, `.` escaped, both anchored). The divergence the reviewer demonstrates needs a mid-pattern `**/` glob, which no entry in ci.ciConfig or CI_DEFINING_PATHS has; list drift is separately pinned by checks.test.mjs:492-551, and definesCi's only consumer runs from a full checkout (agent-review-panel.yml:1475,1508). There is also a structural reason the copy isn't gratuitous: `scripts/agent` is sparse-checked-out alone in eight workflows (agent-review-panel.yml:535-536, agent-rerun.yml:255-256) and no scripts/agent module imports any scripts/*.mjs root module. So the violation is real but its cost stays inside the codebase (a third matcher where an exported one exists, unpinned against it) — no acceptance criterion unmet, no user-visible behavior change, no divergent answers today. Under this lens's rubric that is minor ("reuse that was available but not required" / "wrong layer with no behavioral consequence"), and minor never blocks.
